# Final Touches — Murim Login

## Goal

Prepare one mastered chapter for readers. This pass adds footnotes, repairs formatting, and fixes duplicate or missing sentences. It is not a fluency rewrite.

Keep the mastered prose. Change a sentence only to attach a footnote, repair System / thought / speech / chat formatting, restore a source sentence the English dropped, remove an English sentence the Korean does not support, or fix a character's name or pronoun as described below.

## Names and pronouns

The packet lists the profiled characters named in this chapter with their gender, and any required name corrections.

- Use the glossary or character-card English for every name. Apply each required name correction everywhere it occurs.
- Korean usually omits pronouns. When a card gives `female` or `male` and the English uses the other pronoun for that character, fix the pronoun. Leave pronouns alone for a character whose gender is `unknown`.

## Duplicates and omissions

Compare the English with the Korean source.

- Restore source facts, events, dialogue, and sentences the English dropped, in the same place in the scene.
- Remove English sentences that have no support in the Korean.
- Keep a bold label that names a quoted document, manual, warning, or sign, such as `> **Warning**`. Keep it when this chapter recalls or reprints a notice that was labeled earlier, even if the Korean reprint shows only the body.
- Keep repetition the Korean itself repeats: comedy, panic, emphasis, echoed dialogue, and short beats such as `……`.
- Do not treat a short refrain or a deliberate echo as a duplicate.

## Footnotes

Use Markdown footnotes (`[^1]`, `[^2]`, …). Number them in order of first appearance, starting at 1 for this chapter. Put every definition in one block at the end of the file.

Within this chapter, write one definition for a term, unit, amount, or reference. Every later occurrence of that same thing reuses the same marker. `goshiwon` five times is one note, and so is `hyung`. A different amount or a different term gets its own note. Another chapter may carry its own note for the same term.

Write notes in factual English. No spoilers and no jokes added by the note. Romanize words. A note may include the original character when it is explaining that character. Keep Hangul jamo already used as chat reactions, such as ㅋㅋ and ㄷㄷ.

Never write a footnote whose job is to identify or describe a story character, creature, pet, group, place, item, or plot event. The story introduces its own cast; a note must not say who someone is, what they did, or what a name refers to inside the story. This holds even when the glossary or a character card explains the name: those are reference for you, not footnote material.

When a story name coincides with a real person, brand, or work (Magic Johnson, Mimi), the name is the story's. Do not footnote the real one unless the Korean source itself makes that reference.

Add a note only when an English reader would otherwise miss the meaning or the conversion. Skip it when the sentence already says what the reference means. A translated proverb whose warning is plain, a joke the next line completes, a place name used as a place, and a fictional law the dialogue already describes do not get notes.

Skip a conversion footnote when the prose already states both metric and imperial for that quantity.

### Won

Footnote Korean won, including round figures and vague amounts (“hundreds of millions of won”), when the prose does not already give the conversion. Use only the project rates in the packet. Show dollars, then euros, as approximate figures. Round large amounts to about two significant figures and say “about.” For a vague amount, give the approximate range those words cover. One note per distinct amount; reuse it for every later mention of that same amount.

Do not convert traditional money (nyang, taels, cash) or Chinese yuan with the won rate. Explain those with a cultural or historical note only when the English does not already carry the meaning.

### Units

Footnote a Korean or Chinese traditional unit, or a metric quantity, once in the chapter, with both metric and imperial, using this table:

| Unit | Use | Metric | Imperial |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pyeong (평) | area | 3.31 m² | 35.6 ft² |
| geun (근) | Korean weight | 600 g | 1.32 lb |
| ja / cheok (자) | length | 30.3 cm | 11.9 in |
| chi (치) | length | 3.03 cm | 1.19 in |
| don (돈) | weight | 3.75 g | 0.132 oz |
| gwan (관) | weight | 3.75 kg | 8.27 lb |
| ri (리), Korea | distance | 393 m | 0.244 mi |
| li (里), China | distance | 500 m | 0.311 mi |
| jin (斤), modern Chinese | weight | 500 g | 1.10 lb |
| liang (两), modern Chinese | weight | 50 g | 1.76 oz |

Choose Korean ri or Chinese li from the setting. Say which one the note uses.

Also footnote metric quantities already in the English (kilometers, meters, centimeters, kilograms, grams, liters, square meters, degrees Celsius) with the imperial equivalent. Use unit words or abbreviations (`ft`, `in`, `mi`, `lb`, `oz`, `gal`). Do not use `"` or `'` as unit marks.

### Cultural references

Footnote a Korean, Chinese, or other Asian word, custom, institution, food, joke, or allusion when the English does not already carry it: `goshiwon`, `hyung`, `doenjang`, `jeonse`. Explain it in one or two sentences. One note per term in the chapter, reused by every later occurrence.

Leave it unnoted when the English is already clear. Do not explain a proverb the translation has already stated, a pun the scene completes, or ordinary vocabulary.

Do not footnote standing series vocabulary. Never add a note whose job is to define any of these, including ordinary variants and compounds:

- Murim
- qi, including demonic qi, innate qi, and qi deviation
- dantian, including the Upper, Middle, and Lower Dantian
- internal energy
- mana

A note about something else may mention these words. Do not attach a marker to them.

## Formatting

Enforce these four patterns. Repair System, speech, thought, and chat formatting when it drifts. Leave every other blockquote heading as it stands.

- **System.** Each real game System panel is one Markdown blockquote headed exactly `> **System**`. Keep the panel’s lines inside that blockquote. Start a new panel only when prose intervenes. Keep every `> **System**` panel from the mastered chapter, including a notice the narrator only hears. Do not turn a panel into italics, a sound effect, or narration. Do not repeat a panel. A notice the mastered chapter already shows more than once stays repeated that many times, and no more. Do not wrap System text in square brackets or label a manual, sign, or ordinary quotation as System. A manual or remembered notice keeps its own label, such as `> **Warning**` or `> **Product User Manual**`. That label is not a System panel, and it is not drift.
- **Speech.** Spoken dialogue uses curly double quotes (`“` `”`). Not straight quotes, not italics.
- **Thoughts.** Direct thoughts are italics with no quotation marks. Keep a mastered thought in italics. Do not turn it into spoken dialogue.
- **Chat and comments.** Public comment threads and private chat logs shown as threads are one blockquote. Each message line begins with `└`, as in `> └ **Name:** message`. Keep a thread title that is not itself a message, such as `> **Peace Guild**`, on its own line above the messages. Do not add a `**Chat**` heading. A status line that is only a name or level, such as `> **Lv. 22 Hyuk Mujin**`, is not a chat message. Leave that line unchanged, including the bold. Ordinary spoken dialogue stays in curly quotes.
- **Headings.** The only Markdown heading is `# Chapter N`. Do not add `##` or `###`. A diary title or similar label stays a bold line, `**Training Day 1**`, even when the mastered copy used a smaller heading.

Leave narration as narration. Scene breaks stay `* * *`, with the same count as the source.

## Output contract

Return only the complete English Markdown chapter. The first nonblank line must be `# Chapter N`. No status line and no model preamble. Do not add Hangul syllables. Chat jamo and a character cited in a note may stay.

## Project conversion rates

These rates are binding. Do not look up or substitute a market rate.

- 1 US dollar = 1400 Korean won
- 1 euro = 1550 Korean won

Convert every won amount with these rates. In each footnote, give dollars first and euros second.

그러나 황금빛 눈동자의 인간, 후긴은 아랑곳하지 않고 고개를 돌려 등 뒤의 누군가에게 정중히 고개를 숙였다.

“네임드 몬스터인 자이언트 오우거(Giant Ogre)입니다. 어찌하시겠습니까?”

Like the ancient god whose name they bore: Odin.

*Whooooooosh! Slash!*

A clash. Then a slaughter.

>

Odin.

# Final Touches — Murim Login

## Goal

Prepare one mastered chapter for readers. This pass adds footnotes, repairs formatting, and fixes duplicate or missing sentences. It is not a fluency rewrite.

Keep the mastered prose. Change a sentence only to attach a footnote, repair System / thought / speech / chat formatting, restore a source sentence the English dropped, remove an English sentence the Korean does not support, or fix a character's name or pronoun as described below.

## Names and pronouns

The packet lists the profiled characters named in this chapter with their gender, and any required name corrections.

- Use the glossary or character-card English for every name. Apply each required name correction everywhere it occurs.
- Korean usually omits pronouns. When a card gives `female` or `male` and the English uses the other pronoun for that character, fix the pronoun. Leave pronouns alone for a character whose gender is `unknown`.

## Duplicates and omissions

Compare the English with the Korean source.

- Restore source facts, events, dialogue, and sentences the English dropped, in the same place in the scene.
- Remove English sentences that have no support in the Korean.
- Keep a bold label that names a quoted document, manual, warning, or sign, such as `> **Warning**`. Keep it when this chapter recalls or reprints a notice that was labeled earlier, even if the Korean reprint shows only the body.
- Keep repetition the Korean itself repeats: comedy, panic, emphasis, echoed dialogue, and short beats such as `……`.
- Do not treat a short refrain or a deliberate echo as a duplicate.

## Footnotes

Use Markdown footnotes (`[^1]`, `[^2]`, …). Number them in order of first appearance, starting at 1 for this chapter. Put every definition in one block at the end of the file.

Within this chapter, write one definition for a term, unit, amount, or reference. Every later occurrence of that same thing reuses the same marker. `goshiwon` five times is one note, and so is `hyung`. A different amount or a different term gets its own note. Another chapter may carry its own note for the same term.

Write notes in factual English. No spoilers and no jokes added by the note. Romanize words. A note may include the original character when it is explaining that character. Keep Hangul jamo already used as chat reactions, such as ㅋㅋ and ㄷㄷ.

Never write a footnote whose job is to identify or describe a story character, creature, pet, group, place, item, or plot event. The story introduces its own cast; a note must not say who someone is, what they did, or what a name refers to inside the story. This holds even when the glossary or a character card explains the name: those are reference for you, not footnote material.

When a story name coincides with a real person, brand, or work (Magic Johnson, Mimi), the name is the story's. Do not footnote the real one unless the Korean source itself makes that reference.

Add a note only when an English reader would otherwise miss the meaning or the conversion. Skip it when the sentence already says what the reference means. A translated proverb whose warning is plain, a joke the next line completes, a place name used as a place, and a fictional law the dialogue already describes do not get notes.

Skip a conversion footnote when the prose already states both metric and imperial for that quantity.

### Won

Footnote Korean won, including round figures and vague amounts (“hundreds of millions of won”), when the prose does not already give the conversion. Use only the project rates in the packet. Show dollars, then euros, as approximate figures. Round large amounts to about two significant figures and say “about.” For a vague amount, give the approximate range those words cover. One note per distinct amount; reuse it for every later mention of that same amount.

Do not convert traditional money (nyang, taels, cash) or Chinese yuan with the won rate. Explain those with a cultural or historical note only when the English does not already carry the meaning.

Footnote a Korean or Chinese traditional unit, or a metric quantity, once in the chapter, with both metric and imperial, using this table:

| pyeong (평) | area | 3.31 m² | 35.6 ft² |
| geun (근) | Korean weight | 600 g | 1.32 lb |

Footnote a Korean, Chinese, or other Asian word, custom, institution, food, joke, or allusion when the English does not already carry it: `goshiwon`, `hyung`, `doenjang`, `jeonse`. Explain it in one or two sentences. One note per term in the chapter, reused by every later occurrence.

- Murim
- qi, including demonic qi, innate qi, and qi deviation
- dantian, including the Upper, Middle, and Lower Dantian
- internal energy
- mana

A note about something else may mention these words. Do not attach a marker to them.

## Formatting

Enforce these four patterns. Repair System, speech, thought, and chat formatting when it drifts. Leave every other blockquote heading as it stands.

- **System.** Each real game System panel is one Markdown blockquote headed exactly `> **System**`. Keep the panel’s lines inside that blockquote. Start a new panel only when prose intervenes. Do not wrap System text in square brackets or label a manual, sign, or ordinary quotation as System. - **Headings.** The only Markdown heading is `# Chapter N`. Do not add `##` or `###`. A diary title or similar label stays a bold line, `**Training Day 1**`, even when the mastered copy used a smaller heading.

Leave narration as narration. Scene breaks stay `* * *`, with the same count as the source.

## Output contract

Return only the complete English Markdown chapter. The first nonblank line must be `# Chapter N`. No status line and no model preamble. Do not add Hangul syllables. Chat jamo and a character cited in a note may stay.

These rates are binding. Do not look up or substitute a market rate.

- 1 US dollar = 1400 Korean won
- 1 euro = 1550 Korean won

Convert every won amount with these rates. In each footnote, give dollars first and euros second.

― 경험치가 대폭 하락합니다.

― 명성치가 대폭 하락합니다.

― 특수 칭호, [수수방관(袖手傍觀)]이 향후 30일간 적용됩니다.

― 특수 칭호, [수수방관]의 패널티 효과로 인해 모든 능력치가 10% 하락합니다.

나는 짤막한 신음을 흘렸다.

퀘스트 실패?

막대한 패널티?

그런 것 따위는 아무것도 아니었다.

뒤늦게 우리의 모습을 발견하고 웅성거리기 시작한 주위의 분위기도. 폐허를 가로지르는 일단의 무리도 마찬가지다.

‘죽었다. 전부.’

그것이 현실이었다.

아레스 길드의 파리 지부는 더 이상 존재하지 않는다.

인근에서 평화롭게 하루를 시작하던 사람들도 마찬가지다.

한때 구름과 닿아 있던 마천루(摩天樓)는 죽음만이 내리깔린 폐허가 되었고, 불과 수십 분 전만 하더라도 이곳에서 웃고 떠들던 사람들은 두 번 다시 돌아올 수 없는 강을 건넜다.

지금 내가 바라보고 있는, 건물의 잔해 속에 파묻힌 이름 모를 누군가의 시신처럼.

무슨 생각이었을까.

멍하니 이름 모를 시신을 내려다보던 나는 불현듯 손을 뻗어 그의 팔을 붙잡았고, 잡아당긴 후에야 또 다른 시신의 팔이라는 것을 깨달았다.

그것이 끝이 아니다.

하나의 시신을 끌어 올리면 세 구의 시신이 보였고, 그들마저 끌어올리면 몸에서 떨어져 나간 사지(四肢)들이 모습을 드러냈다.

“어, 어떻게.”

“간악한 인간이여. 이건, 이건 정말…….”

멀게만 느껴지는 최 팀장과 스켈레톤 킹의 목소리를 들으며, 나는 말 없이 주위를 둘러보았다.

그렇다면 내가 딛고 선 이 폐허 밑에는, 얼마나 많은 이들이 잠들어 있을까.

그리고 그들은 왜.

불덩이를 삼킨 것처럼 뱃속이 뜨겁다.

# Chapter 736

It started with barely a tremor. Nothing more, nothing less.

But that was only the first sign.

*Rumble…*

The ground shook.

Visitors lined up outside the Louvre ducked instinctively. In Paris’s 10th arrondissement, people who had been fighting with fistfuls of each other’s collars broke apart and scattered, swearing as they ran.

And in the 6th arrondissement…

“Ah…”

People forgot to scream. They could only stare, dazed, at the sight before them.

*Gooooom.*

Crimson-black darkness coiled around a skyscraper that rose to a dizzying height, then surged upward.

Everyone held their breath at the vast, ominous energy, unlike anything they had ever felt.

*BOOOOOM!*

The skyscraper that had housed Ares Guild’s Paris branch exploded.

The layers of defensive Magic around its exterior. The sturdy frame built to withstand a missile strike. All of it shattered and burst outward.

Fragments large and small, once part of a building some fifty stories tall, rained down in flames.

*Fwoosh. Whoooooosh!*

“……!”

It was impossible to believe. Impossible to deny.

As countless fragments blotted out the sky, a thought came to the people below.

*Maybe today is the day of the apocalypse described in the Bible.*

Then they saw the air twisting out of shape, and suspicion hardened into despairing certainty.

*Fwoooooosh!*

None of them had ever seen it happen. But as people living amid the brightest civilization in history, they knew what the phenomenon was called.

“Monster Wave…”

The words escaped someone like a groan.

Yet even with debris falling toward them and monsters emerging from the warped space, no one ran.

Not the Sorbonne students cycling to class. Not the young couple walking through the Luxembourg Gardens with a stroller. Not the police rushing to calm the public.

Everyone who had been going about their morning—the entire 6th arrondissement—froze where they stood, gripped by fear and a chill that sank into their bones.

And then—

*BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!*

A rain of fire engulfed everything within a radius of over a hundred meters, and the gates of hell opened.

*Thud. Thud.*

Huge monsters with arms and legs as thick as temple pillars, each with two heads on a single body, beat their chests and roared.

—Gwooooooar!

*Crash!*

Glass shattered all around them, unable to withstand the force of their roars.

Fear, which only powerful monsters could emit, shot out like invisible ropes and bound thousands of people in place.

—Grrrr.

A growl rich with satisfaction.

The hunt was about to begin.

Or so it should have been.

*Whoooooosh! Boom!*

A flash struck the monster at the front, sending it staggering. Everything above its shoulders was gone.

*Thud!*

The ground shook. The hundred or so monsters raised their heads as one.

Among the thousands of people rooted to the spot, predators hidden in the flock of sheep were revealing themselves.

They came with dazzling flashes too fast for the eye to follow.

*Whoooooosh! Crack!*

*Rattle, rattle.*

Flesh and bone crumpled. Blue blood sprayed in every direction.

A Twin Head Ogre that had survived at the cost of one of its heads stepped backward without realizing it.

It had no idea what waited behind it.

*Crunch!*

A gigantic fist burst its remaining head like a watermelon.

The giant possessed strength and a physique far beyond those of the other ogres. It licked its subordinate’s brain matter from its fist, and a golden-eyed human was reflected in its enormous pupils.

—Karsh. Marto.

The words were in the Demon Realm language. They sounded almost like a curse.

Huginn paid them no attention. He turned and bowed politely to someone behind him.

“It is a Named Monster—a Giant Ogre. What would you like to do?”

A calm voice answered.

“Not bad. This should do for a demonstration.”

“Then…?”

“I’ll take it. Clear out the rest.”

That was all.

At the order, Huginn and a hundred Hunters swept forward as one, like the storm and lightning painted on their armor.

Like the ancient god whose name they bore: Odin.

*Whooooooosh! Slash!*

A clash. Then a slaughter.

Limbs as thick as logs flew through the air, and dazzling aura cut through the magical power surging around the monsters.

It was a scene out of myth.

And even in a myth crowded with figures, there was always one hero who shone above the rest.

—Gwooooooar!

*Crack!*

One Strike.

The roar that had seemed ready to swallow the city fell silent.

*Ruuuuumble!*

The Giant Ogre, dozens of meters tall, dropped to its knees before a human who looked tiny beside its mountain of a body.

But to the people who had seen it all, that human was anything but small.

A hero had protected them. A true giant stood before them.

Brought back from the brink of death, the crowd cried out the hero’s name—or the heroes’ names—as one.

“Michael! Michael!”

“Odin Guild!”

As the cheers spread like wildfire, Michael declared in a ringing voice, “Rest assured. As long as Odin Guild and I are here to protect you, no danger will come to you.”

Then he looked toward the ruins beneath the heaps of concrete and added, too quietly for anyone to hear, “At least not today.”

With a faint smile, he stepped toward the remaining monsters, trampling the fallen name *Ares* beneath his foot. The letters had lost their shine when they tore free of the building and fell among the rubble.

* * *

**Odin Guild Declares Support for Ares**

**Odin Guild Master Michael Silbert: “We Offer Our Heartfelt Applause for Ares Guild’s Actions in the Public Interest and Will Walk Forward Alongside Them”**

**Odin Guild Makes Surprise Release of New Mana Cultivation Method!**

**Senior Odin Guild Official Dismisses Pre-Release Controversy: “A Major Project Years in the Making. If You Think We Released It Because of Public Opinion, That Is Regrettable, but We Will Endure It…”**

The breaking news I’d learned from the Skeleton King early that morning had been startling enough.

Before the shock could fade, another wave hit us.

A far bigger, more terrifying one.

*Bzzzt. Bzzzt.*

Team Leader Choi’s smartphone vibrated on the table.

A few seconds later, another breaking report came over the holographic TV. It was hard to believe.

—A Monster Wave has occurred in Paris, France. The site is a skyscraper in the city’s 6th arrondissement, now identified as Ares Guild’s Paris branch, in a shocking development…

—The French government has begun sealing off the 6th arrondissement under international emergency law. The casualty count and details of the operation to suppress the monsters remain unknown…

—Local witnesses say Odin Guild, based nearby, was the first to head to the scene…

Reports poured from the TVs around the restaurant.

But among the countless words spilling from the lips of people with different skin colors and speaking different languages, only three terms pierced my ears.

Monster Wave.

Ares Guild’s Paris branch.

And…

Odin.

*Ding.*

> **System**
>
> A sudden Quest, **The Darkness Over Paris**, has been generated!
>
> You cannot choose whether to accept this Quest. By the authority of the System, the Quest will proceed by force!
>
> **Quest**
>
> **The Darkness Over Paris**
>
> Every choice has consequences.
>
> Your enemies have brought down Ares Guild’s Paris branch, and the city once full of life is now shrouded in darkness and the roars of monsters.
>
> Rescue them as quickly as possible and repel the monster army to prevent innocent casualties!
>
> **Grade:** Supreme Peak
>
> **Restriction:** Jin Taekyung
>
> **Mission:**
>
> Rescue the survivors of the Paris branch (Incomplete)
>
> Suppress the Monster Wave (Incomplete)
>
> **Reward:** Determined by the outcome
>
> **Failure:** Determined by the outcome

“……!”

Everything came at once: the System notification ringing in my ears, the holographic windows appearing before my eyes.

But by the time I saw and heard them, I was already moving on instinct.

No. We all were.

“Gather around me. Quickly!”

Team Leader Choi shouted, pulled a Magic Scroll from his coat, and tore it.

*Fwoosh!*

A blinding flash burst out and enveloped us.

* * *

*If I can’t come help and you need to get somewhere fast, use this. As long as you know the exact coordinates, you’ll arrive safely.*

Magic Johnson had said that when he gave me the Magic Scrolls several weeks ago, near the end of the Middle East cleanup operation.

Now we were burning through the several dozen Teleport scrolls he’d given me, one every few seconds.

*Rip!*

The tough, specially treated parchment tore. The mana dormant inside it awakened, and another brilliant flash enveloped us and carried us toward the chosen coordinates.

*Flash!*

Light flared again and again.

We leaped through space without pause—sometimes tens of kilometers, sometimes hundreds. Before long, my body began to ache, and exhaustion weighed on my mind.

*Hup.*

The rapid succession of spatial-transit spells was taking its toll.

But no one stopped. Not even Team Leader Choi, who was probably bearing the worst of it.

*Grind.*

He clenched his teeth and pulled out another scroll.

Ignoring the foreign airport Hunters thrown into confusion by our unauthorized spatial movement, he tore one scroll, then another before the aftereffects of the first had even faded.

Scroll after scroll ripped apart.

With every flash, the scenery changed. So did the skin colors and languages of the people around us.

At last, after a flash I had long since lost count of, we saw it.

The ruins of what had been Ares Guild’s Paris branch.

Huge monster corpses lay scattered everywhere. Amid the concrete and rebar, I could not sense so much as a trace of life.

Then a sound only I could hear cut through the air.

*Beep.*

> **System**
>
> You have not completed a single mission.
>
> The sudden Quest, **The Darkness Over Paris**, has failed.
>
> Every event brings both reward and cost. You will receive penalties for failing the Quest.
>
> EXP decreases drastically.
>
> Fame decreases drastically.
>
> The special Title **Idle Bystander** will apply for the next 30 days.
>
> Due to the penalty effect of the special Title **Idle Bystander**, all stats decrease by 10%.

“……Ah.”

A small sound escaped me.

Quest failure? A massive penalty?

None of that mattered.

Neither did the murmurs of the people who had belatedly noticed us, or the group making its way across the ruins.

Of all the holographic windows floating before me, my senses fixed on one line.

> **System**
>
> You have not completed a single mission.

That was all.

The cold, rigid sentence bored through my eyes and into my mind. I already knew what it meant.

*They’re dead. All of them.*

That was the reality before me.

Ares Guild’s Paris branch no longer existed. Neither did the people who had begun their day peacefully nearby.

The skyscraper that had once reached the clouds had become a ruin blanketed in death, and the people who had been laughing and talking here only a few dozen minutes ago had crossed a river from which they could never return.

Like the unidentified body buried beneath the wreckage in front of me.

*What was I thinking?*

I stared down at it, then reached out and grabbed an arm. Only when I pulled did I realize the arm belonged to another body.

That wasn’t the end.

When I dragged one body free, I found three more. When I pulled those out, severed limbs emerged beneath them.

“H-how…”

“Wicked human. This… this is truly…”

Team Leader Choi and the Skeleton King sounded impossibly far away. I looked around without a word.

The streets around the former branch had been devastated. Acrid smoke rose, carrying the smell of burning flesh. Bodies not yet recovered lay everywhere.

How many more lay beneath the rubble under my feet?

And why?

*Why did they have to die?*

My stomach burned as though I’d swallowed a ball of fire.

I clenched my teeth until they felt ready to break. Swallowing the blood from my split lips, I struggled to calm the three jiazi of Scorching Yang Qi raging in my dantian.

I could not get any more agitated. I had to remain calm and composed—more than ever.

Otherwise, I wouldn’t be able to face the owner of the immense energy approaching behind me in my right mind.

*Michael Silbert.*

With his name in my thoughts, I slowly turned around.

As the cheers spread like wildfire, Michael declared in a ringing voice, “Rest assured. As long as Odin Guild and I are here to protect you, no danger will come to you.”

Then he looked toward the ruins beneath the heaps of concrete and added, too quietly for anyone to hear, “At least not today.”

With a faint smile, he stepped toward the remaining monsters, trampling the fallen name *Ares* beneath his foot. The letters had lost their shine when they tore free of the building and fell among the rubble.

**Odin Guild Master Michael Silbert: “We Offer Our Heartfelt Applause for Ares Guild’s Actions in the Public Interest and Will Walk Forward Alongside Them”**

The breaking news I’d learned from the Skeleton King early that morning had been startling enough.

Before the shock could fade, another wave hit us.

A far bigger, more terrifying one.

*Bzzzt. Bzzzt.*

Team Leader Choi’s smartphone vibrated on the table.

A few seconds later, another breaking report came over the holographic TV. It was hard to believe.

—A Monster Wave has occurred in Paris, France. The site is a skyscraper in the city’s 6th arrondissement, now identified as Ares Guild’s Paris branch, in a shocking development…

—The French government has begun sealing off the 6th arrondissement under international emergency law. The casualty count and details of the operation to suppress the monsters remain unknown…

—Local witnesses say Odin Guild, based nearby, was the first to head to the scene…

Reports poured from the TVs around the restaurant.

But among the countless words spilling from the lips of people with different skin colors and speaking different languages, only three terms pierced my ears.

Monster Wave.

Ares Guild’s Paris branch.

And…

Odin.

*Ding.*

“……!”

Everything came at once: the System notification ringing in my ears, the holographic windows appearing before my eyes.

But by the time I saw and heard them, I was already moving on instinct.

No. We all were.

“Gather around me. Quickly!”

Team Leader Choi shouted, pulled a Magic Scroll from his coat, and tore it.

*Fwoosh!*

A blinding flash burst out and enveloped us.

*If I can’t come help and you need to get somewhere fast, use this. As long as you know the exact coordinates, you’ll arrive safely.*

Magic Johnson had said that when he gave me the Magic Scrolls several weeks ago, near the end of the Middle East cleanup operation.

Now we were burning through the several dozen Teleport scrolls he’d given me, one every few seconds.

*Rip!*

The tough, specially treated parchment tore. The mana dormant inside it awakened, and another brilliant flash enveloped us and carried us toward the chosen coordinates.

*Flash!*

Light flared again and again.

We leaped through space without pause—sometimes tens of kilometers,[^3] sometimes hundreds.[^4] Before long, my body began to ache, and exhaustion weighed on my mind.

*Hup.*

The rapid succession of spatial-transit spells was taking its toll.

But no one stopped. Not even Team Leader Choi, who was probably bearing the worst of it.

*Grind.*

He clenched his teeth and pulled out another scroll.

Ignoring the foreign airport Hunters thrown into confusion by our unauthorized spatial movement, he tore one scroll, then another before the aftereffects of the first had even faded.

Scroll after scroll ripped apart.

With every flash, the scenery changed. So did the skin colors and languages of the people around us.

At last, after a flash I had long since lost count of, we saw it.

The ruins of what had been Ares Guild’s Paris branch.

Huge monster corpses lay scattered everywhere. Amid the concrete and rebar, I could not sense so much as a trace of life.

Then a sound only I could hear cut through the air.

*Beep.*

> **System**
>
> You have not completed a single mission.
>
> The sudden Quest, **The Darkness Over Paris**, has failed.
>
> Every event brings both reward and cost. You will receive penalties for failing the Quest.
>
> EXP decreases drastically.
>
> Fame decreases drastically.
>

>
> Due to the penalty effect of the special Title **Idle Bystander**, all stats decrease by 10%.

“……Ah.”

A small sound escaped me.

Quest failure? A massive penalty?

None of that mattered.

Neither did the murmurs of the people who had belatedly noticed us, or the group making its way across the ruins.

Of all the holographic windows floating before me, my senses fixed on one line.

> **System**
>
> You have not completed a single mission.

That was all.

The cold, rigid sentence bored through my eyes and into my mind. I already knew what it meant.

*They’re dead. All of them.*

That was the reality before me.

Ares Guild’s Paris branch no longer existed. Neither did the people who had begun their day peacefully nearby.

The skyscraper that had once reached the clouds had become a ruin blanketed in death, and the people who had been laughing and talking here only a few dozen minutes ago had crossed a river from which they could never return.

Like the unidentified body buried beneath the wreckage in front of me.

*What was I thinking?*

I stared down at it, then reached out and grabbed an arm. Only when I pulled did I realize the arm belonged to another body.

That wasn’t the end.

When I dragged one body free, I found three more. When I pulled those out, severed limbs emerged beneath them.

“H-how…”

“Wicked human. This… this is truly…”

Team Leader Choi and the Skeleton King sounded impossibly far away. I looked around without a word.

The streets around the former branch had been devastated. Acrid smoke rose, carrying the smell of burning flesh. Bodies not yet recovered lay everywhere.

How many more lay beneath the rubble under my feet?

And why?

*Why did they have to die?*

My stomach burned as though I’d swallowed a ball of fire.

I clenched my teeth until they felt ready to break. Swallowing the blood from my split lips, I struggled to calm the three jiazi[^5] of Scorching Yang Qi raging in my dantian.

I could not get any more agitated. I had to remain calm and composed—more than ever.

Otherwise, I wouldn’t be able to face the owner of the immense energy approaching behind me in my right mind.

*Michael Silbert.*

With his name in my thoughts, I slowly turned around.
